_source.what: Oracle answers for the in-house fraud QPP suite. The generator is deterministic per seed, so the planted rings are known before the query runs — an engine-independent oracle, stronger than engine-self-reporting.

checks.planted-ring: the generator's planted directed cycle (cycle-0, cycle-1, ...) must appear among the returned rings, starting at its first account and closed; accidental noise rings may appear beside it, the planted one may not be missing. Runs over the graph generated with the datasets crate's fraud generator.
checks.rows: exact rows, compared with the graph-benchmark-ldbc lane's no-coercion rules (answers::compare). Runs over the workload's sample fixture (fixture-f06.cypher).
checks.none: no answer check; a kept entry whose oracle is the prose notes recorded here.

_source.generator: the existing relate-datasets fraud generator (monopartite Account/TRANSFER, planted 'fanout'/'cycle'), driven at its CI scale (FraudConfig::ci(): scale 0.05, seed 42, fanout_k 12, cycle_len 4). The bipartite (FROM/TO) and needle generators the f03-f05 drafts target are follow-up work; those entries stay kept until they exist.
_source.spike_reference_points: 2026-10-31 spike against the (unlicensed, never-to-be-committed) external dataset: 8 rings on the bipartite 20%-rule bounded {1,6} (5.9 s, 617 MB, matches the stated blog oracle); the 1000->900->810->729 sample ring; 5 date-ordered cycles hand-enumerated. The in-house generator must reproduce comparable shapes and counts at its default scale. These are facts, not expression (license-notes.md §4).

f01-monopartite-cycle.note: the planted cycle account ids, stable per generator seed (the generator prints them and the runner reads them from its output)

f02-simple-cycle.note: the same planted cycle as f01 — SIMPLE never removes a planted simple ring

f03-bipartite-bounded-ring.note: kept: the bipartite generator is follow-up work; the oracle will be its planted ring ids (8 rings at the default scale)

f04-bipartite-unbounded.note: kept: the unbounded + form does not terminate today (no walk budget, no frontier kernel); frontier-NFA acceptance case (LABS-644) and the walk-budget case (LABS-660 item 3)

f05-needle.note: kept: the needle generator is follow-up work; the oracle will be exactly the planted ring, ids needle-0..needle-(N-1) in order

f06-sample-ring.note: exactly one ring; nodes(p) lists the closed endpoint twice, so the ring column is 1-2-3-4-1
